summary: Stale IdP claim cache causes 403s on k8s dashboard after Okta group changes
description: Issue summary: After a recent Okta group membership change for several platform engineers, affected users received 403 Forbidden when opening the Kubernetes dashboard. Impact: Blocks developer access to the k8s-dashboard for the platform and infra teams during a canary rollout; several CI jobs that rely on service accounts to query the dashboard metrics also failed. Scope: ~8 users reported, intermittent depending on whether they authenticated through the identity-proxy with a cached claim. Observed behavior: identity-proxy appears to be returning stale 'groups' claim from cache for up to 5 minutes after Okta membership updates. Expected behavior: role mappings should reflect Okta group changes within seconds of the IdP notification or an explicit SCIM webhook.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Remove or add user to Okta group 'platform-engineers' via Okta admin console
2) Wait for Okta incremental sync (or trigger manual SCIM update), note timestamp in Okta log
3) Immediately sign in to console/grafana/k8s-dashboard using SSO (identity-proxy path)
4) Observe 403 on k8s-dashboard despite Okta showing new group membership
5) After ~5 minutes (cache TTL) repeat sign-in and access is restored
logs: identity-proxy (pod auth-proxy-7b6c): INFO 2024-08-15T09:42:10Z returning cached claims for user=ashapatel (cache_key=idp_claims:U12345, ttl=298s)
k8s-dashboard: 2024-08-15T09:42:12Z 403 Forbidden for user=ashapatel (role mapping lookup failed for groups=[old-group])
Okta system log: 2024-08-15T09:41:58Z User U12345 added to group 'platform-engineers' (source=SCIM)
comments: Support (Asha): Customer-facing users alerted infra that several engineers couldn't access the k8s dashboard after I moved them between Okta groups. Creating ticket to track cause and fix.
SRE (Ethan): Confirmed 403 reproducer locally. Identity-proxy cache returns stale groups claim when Okta sends SCIM changes. Investigating cache invalidation path.

Platform (Maya): We saw failing CI tasks that read the dashboard metrics using the same session tokens. Workaround request: can we provide a cache-bust endpoint or invalidate specific keys for affected users?
SRE (Ethan): Temporary mitigation deployed: added admin endpoint to purge idp_claims:<user_id> from memcached. Running entitlement purge for affected 8 users. Need permanent fix.
Security (Jon): Are there any auth bypass risks with the admin purge endpoint? Please add audit logging and restrict to internal service account.
Ethan: Audit logging added, endpoint restricted to svc-auth-maintainer. Patching identity-proxy to check 'groups_version' claim and accept a per-user versioning header from Okta webhook.
Maya: Confirmed access restored for the 8 impacted engineers post-purge. Monitoring for reoccurrence.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: identity-proxy caches full id_token claims keyed by user id for 300s to reduce IdP calls. Okta group delta updates happen outside the token lifecycle; there's no invalidation on SCIM webhook currently.
Checked memcached keys: found idp_claims:U12345 with value groups=[old-group] and ttl remaining ~290s right after Okta event timestamp.
Looked at identity-proxy code path: cache write occurs on token exchange; the SCIM webhook handler does not trigger cache invalidation.
Reproduced in staging by adding/removing group and calling dashboard immediately: identical 403 and cached claim observed.
Related configs: cache TTL set to 300s in Helm values (values.yaml: identityProxy.cache.ttlSeconds: 300).
resolution: Workaround applied (short-term): added an authenticated admin endpoint svc-auth-maintainer/purge-cache that deletes idp_claims:<user_id> keys from memcached; used to restore access for 8 users immediately.

Permanent fix (in progress): PR 468 updates identity-proxy to a) include groups_version in cached payload, b) consult Okta webhook 'groups_version' header and invalidate cache for that user if webhook version > cached version, and c) reduce default cache TTL to 60s for interactive sessions.

Rollout plan: merge to main -> staged rollout to staging (done), canary to 10% prod nodes (monitor 15m), full rollout if no regressions. Add automated cache invalidation invocation from SCIM webhook path.

Postmortem action items: 1) Add end-to-end test for group-change -> immediate access; 2) Update runbook with cache-bust playbook and who can call the admin endpoint; 3) Instrument metrics for idp_cache_hit/miss and webhook-triggered invalidations.
Status: Mitigation applied and PR open; target to close ticket after full prod rollout and 24h stability window.
